title: Why Children Blink Excessively | Top Reasons and Remedies Explained
description: It's worrying to see your child blinking frequently and forcefully without knowing what's wrong. asr.full_text: Hi, welcome to another eye health episode on my channel. In today's video, we're going to be addressing a phenomenon that is found in children a little more. Commonly than you might think. That is excessive blinking. Want to know the possible causes and. How to fix them? Stick around. If I ask you, you probably can recall a child that you know or have. Come across that blinks a little more hard and frequently than usual. Yes, it. Can be a facial tick, but I certainly wouldn't jump to any conclusions without. Having it properly checked with an optometrist. More often than not, from my. Experience, there is a direct ocular cause. Just off the top of my head, there. Are three main causes of excessive blinking in children that I definitely. Would want to rule out first. Number one, dry eyes. Now this is possibly the most common cause. And for good reason. Studies show we blink only half the amount that we normally do when we're. Engaged in staring activities such as reading a book or staring at digital devices. Blinks are. Very important in helping to spread the tears evenly over our eyes and to pump oils from oil. Glands lining our lids to help moisturize the eyes. When we fail to do so or don't do it enough,. Our eyes are going to be irritated. Now adults deal with this problem too, but we're better at. Recognizing the problem and know to take breaks. Children, on the other hand, have more difficulty. Recognizing the problem and they only compensate with increased heart blinks as an after response. Now, one way to tell if excessive blinking is due to the dryness is to see if the child's. Blinking is worse after they've been engaged in staring activities and presents as normal. The rest of the time. Ways to avoid excessive blinking due to dryness is to limit screen time, remind them to blink. When you catch them staring for too long, and you can go as far as to introducing a. Humidifier and artificial tears, but really the problem should resolve in most cases with the. Previous suggestions. The second possible cause of excessive blinking in children is interned lashes. This is a cause that is often overlooked but is really simple to rectify. Children may naturally. Have misdirected lashes that point towards the eyes and rub against it such that it's irritating. Now depending on the severity, it may not register as pain to them so they don't complain,. But they do show their discomfort through increased blinking. Children with misdirected lashes tend to blink on a more consistent basis rather than having. It being worse after they've engaged in a specific activity. You may be able to directly see the misdirected lashes, but since lashes are quite fine, the. Best way to make a proper diagnosis is to have the optometrist check it out with equipment. That can magnify the view by many times over. The quickest, most effective method to solve the problem is to remove the misdirected lashes. In clinic. I wouldn't recommend you trying at home because without the proper equipment, you may do more. Damage than help for the child. Now also have your child refrain from eye rubbing because that can exacerbate the interning. Of the lashes toward the eyes. Another good trick is to use a wet towel. To lightly brush the child's lashes away from their eyes. As they look the opposite way. So if you're going to brush the lower lashes,. Have them look up and do it very carefully. Making sure to pull the lids a little ways away. From the eye is going to prevent direct contact. Of the towel with the eyes. The third possible cause of excessive blinking in children. Is allergic conjunctivitis. Under the big umbrella of allergic conjunctivitis. Are two main types that can cause. Excessive blinking in children. Acute allergic conjunctivitis and vernal conjunctivitis. The two are not that easy to tell apart. At first glance, they have many similar symptoms. Such as redness, watering, and itching of the eyes. Now, without getting too technical,. I'm going to tell you the main ways that you can get a hunch on which type your child has. Aside from the ocular symptoms, acute allergic conjunctivitis is often associated with hallmark. Signs such as sneezing and nasal discharge. It has very little long-term effect on eye health. And vision, and it's usually effectively managed with anti-allergy eye drops and or oral. Antihistamines. Vernal conjunctivitis, on the other hand, is more associated with children. With pre-existing conditions of asthma, dermatitis, and eczema. In many cases, other than the. Anti-allergy medications, a steroid eye drop may need to be added for effective control of. Moderate to severe cases. If left untreated, some of these cases can take on a more chronic form,. Leading to permanent changes and scarring of eye structures, which ultimately can cause vision. Impairment. It is only after I have ruled out the above conditions would I consider that a child's. Excessive blinking to be possibly due to a facial tick or of a neurotic nature. If in doubt, check. With your local optometrist first. If you know a child who has excessive blinking, make sure to. Pass this video along to his or her parents because children may not always know how to. Express themselves. A simple visit with the optometrist may be all that's needed to find. And fix the problem. If you took something away from today's video, I would appreciate if you hit. That like button, consider subscribing, hit that notification bell so that you won't miss the next. Video. Until then, I'll see you in the next one. Bye! I do! Ahhh! I do!
